sources.entry: PDF Archiver - Nice tool for tagging and archiving tasks. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/JulianKahnert/PDF-Archiver) [![App Store][app-store Icon]](https://apps.apple.com/app/pdf-archivar/id1352719750?platform=mac)

summary.one_liner: PDF Archiver is a macOS and iOS app for tagging, naming, and archiving scanned documents so they can be searched by tag, description, or content.
summary.what_it_does: The app moves documents from an untagged folder into a Archive folder organized by year after you tag them. Files follow a naming convention: a yyyy-mm-dd date, a description, and tags, such as "2017-05-12--apple-macbook__apple_bill.pdf". Capital letters, spaces, and language-specific characters are stripped from names for filesystem compatibility. The README says the archive layout is independent of OS and filesystem, and that you can search by tag (prefix "_"), by description (prefix "-"), or by any plain word. A companion PDF Archiver for iOS app is used to scan documents and get text-recognition-based tag and date suggestions. The README also mentions searching file content through the Pro Tips, which are not detailed there. The app is distributed through the App Store, and the repository includes instructions for cloning and building it with Xcode.
use_cases: archive scanned bills and letters digitally
tag and rename PDF documents with a consistent naming scheme
organize paper documents into yearly digital archives
search archived PDFs by tag or description
scan documents on iPhone and file them on a Mac
how_to_run: Install PDF Archiver from the Mac App Store or the App Store
Or clone the repository: git clone (URL as given in README)
Build and run the PDF Archiver target
notable: Filenames encode date, description, and tags so archives stay searchable without a database
Companion iOS app adds scanning with text recognition and tag/date suggestions
Archive structure is independent of OS and filesystem
caveats: Core features depend on the separate iOS companion app for scanning
README does not state platform minimum versions or a license
